title: The Disagreement Problem in Explainable Machine Learning: A Practitioner's Perspective
authors: Krishna S; Han T; Gu A; Pombra J; Jabbari S; Wu ZS; Lakkaraju H
task: Disagreement between post-hoc explanation methods (tabular benchmarks)
method: Formalises disagreement of explanations (feature ranking / direction) and surveys practitioners
stability_definition: Rank/sign agreement metrics between explainers on one model
validation: Empirical on standard tabular datasets; practitioner interviews
limitations_or_relevance: Explanations often disagree in importance ranking and direction; practitioners resolve disagreement heuristically
relevance_to_bioxplain: General ML (not transcriptomics; no resampling stability or external cohort)
overlaps_or_challenges_novelty: Direct precedent for the explainer-dimension result (linear coef vs SHAP vs permutation top sets barely overlap). BioXplain adds resampling stability with chance correction and cross-cohort replication in a high-dimensional omics setting
verification_level: PARTIAL - explainer disagreement is a known phenomenon

title: Stability of Feature Selection in Multi-Omics Data Analysis
method: Stability measured with 5-fold CV across classifiers and regularisation strengths
limitations_or_relevance: Snippet: stability improved with stronger regularisation and dropped with weaker regularisation across classifiers
relevance_to_bioxplain: Supports (qualitatively) our regularisation-sensitivity theme; our own result is non-monotone (C=1 lowest)

title: A Stability-Oriented Biomarker Selection Framework Synergistically Driven by Robust Rank Aggregation and L1-Sparse Modeling
